newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Audiolux investors urged to stay - paper.
newsitem.headline: Audiolux investors urged to stay - paper.

text.p: Private investors in Luxembourg media holding Audiolux should stick with the company and not take up an offer later this month to swap their interests for a stake in Audiofina, Audiolux's controlling shareholder was quoted as saying on Thursday.
"The public has every interest in staying in Audiolux," Gaston Schwertzer, chief executive officer of Luxempart SA, told the Luxemburger Wort newspaper.

"Audiolux is a quoted company with an excellent reputation. Our objective will be to diversify its asset base to include other audiovisual companies, either from Luxembourg or elsewhere," Schwertzer added.

Holding company Luxempart is Audiolux's biggest shareholder with 30 percent, followed by Banque Generale Luxembourg (15 percent), Paribas Luxembourg (14 percent), BCEE (12 percent), SNCI (12 percent), Le Foyer (5 percent) and La Luxembourgeoise (3 percent). Around eight percent is listed.

Audiolux has convened an extraordinary general shareholders' meeting for March 14 at which institutional shareholders will receive 19 Audiofina shares plus cash per Audiolux share they hold as part of a reduction in the company's capital.
Audiofina is a holding company that owns 50 percent of CLT-UFA, Europe's largest terrestrial broadcasting company.
The Wort newspaper cited an unnamed official from state holding company SNCI as saying all the institutional investors would take part in the exchange.
The newspaper speculated whether Luxempart would sell Audiolux its 3.59 percent in unlisted Societe Europeenne des Satellites, the Luxembourg operator of Astra satellites.
Schwertzer declined to comment, it said.
Audiofina is itself controlled by companies linked to Belgium's Groupe Bruxelles Lambert SA. The remaining 50 percent of CLT-UFA is owned by Germany's Bertelsmann group.
